label: Stop Prolonged Beyond Its Original Purpose

trigger.description: Ask whenever there was a traffic or investigative stop, to determine whether it was extended beyond the time reasonably required for its original purpose.

non_gating_questions.q_stop_type: Used only to route which vehicle-stop-timeline questions get asked at all (decision-tree concern) — not part of this issue's match condition.

review_conditions.display_note: It's unclear whether the officer developed independent reasonable suspicion during the original-purpose tasks. If it turns out suspicion did arise then, the extension may be independently justified and this issue could be weaker than presented — confirm the timeline (dispatch log, body-cam) before relying on this issue as written.

rule_statements.text: A traffic stop becomes unlawful if it is prolonged beyond the time reasonably required to complete the mission of the stop.

Authority for the seizure ends when tasks tied to the traffic infraction are, or reasonably should have been, completed, and an officer may not extend an otherwise-completed stop, even briefly, to conduct a dog sniff or other unrelated investigation absent independent reasonable suspicion.
A dog sniff is permissible only if it does not add time to the stop.

Where an officer develops reasonable, articulable suspicion of additional criminal activity during the stop's original mission, a brief extension to investigate that suspicion may be justified; the burden is on the government to establish that suspicion arose before, not after, the original mission concluded.

practice_notes: Rodriguez rejects a bright-line minimum delay — even a short, unjustified extension can violate the Fourth Amendment, so don't discount this issue just because the added time was brief.
Get the dispatch log and any body-cam/dash-cam timestamps in discovery early — this issue lives and dies on minute-by-minute sequencing.
Pin down the officer's own testimony on when each original-purpose task was completed; officers sometimes pad task completion time in reports to avoid a Rodriguez problem.
If a K-9 unit was called before the original tasks were done, that timing itself can be favorable — it suggests intent to prolong regardless of what happened later.
